n: Moroni now addresses those who do not believe in Christ. This chapter is his powerful testimony to skeptics of every age.
He asks: when the Lord comes and the earth is rolled up and the elements melt, when you stand before the Lamb of God — will you still say there is no God?

f.g: The time when God comes to judge or bless.

f.w: the elements shall melt with fervent heat

n: Will you still deny Christ then? Could you even bear to look at him? Do you think you could be happy living with a holy Being while tormented by awareness of having broken his laws?
Moroni says such a person would be more miserable living with a holy God than with the damned in hell. Heaven would not feel like heaven to an unrepentant heart.

f.w: more miserable to dwell with a holy and just God

n: Seeing your own spiritual nakedness beside God’s glory and Christ’s holiness would be like an unquenchable fire. The “fire” is in part the burning awareness of guilt.

f.g: Being fully exposed, with nothing hidden.

n: So turn to the Lord now, cry mightily to the Father in Jesus’ name, and perhaps you can be found spotless, pure, and white, cleansed by the Lamb’s blood at the last day.

f.w: cleansed by the blood of the Lamb

n: Next Moroni speaks to those who say revelation, prophecy, spiritual gifts, healing, and tongues have ceased.
Whoever denies these things doesn’t know the gospel — he either hasn’t read the scriptures or doesn’t understand them.

f.w: knoweth not the gospel of Christ

n: Scripture teaches that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, with no variation or shadow of change.

f.w: the same yesterday, today, and forever
no variableness neither shadow of changing

n: If you imagine a God who changes, you have invented a god who is not a God of miracles. The real God does not change his nature.

f.g: Made up in your own minds.

n: Moroni will show them the God of miracles: the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who created the heavens, the earth, and everything in them.

f.w: the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob

n: God created Adam; through Adam came the Fall; because of the Fall came Jesus Christ, “the Father and the Son”; and through Christ came redemption. It is the plan of salvation in one verse.

f.w: by Adam came the fall of man

f.g: Christ is called Father as Creator and as the one who gives us new birth, and Son because of his mortal body.

n: Through redemption all people return to God’s presence. Christ’s death brings resurrection, waking all from the “endless sleep” when the trumpet sounds; all will stand at his judgment bar, freed from physical death.

f.g: His judgment seat, like a court.

n: Then comes judgment, and people remain what they have become: the filthy stay filthy, the righteous stay righteous, the happy stay happy.

f.w: he that is filthy shall be filthy still

n: To those who believe in a God who cannot do miracles: has the end come yet? No — so God has not stopped being a God of miracles.
Aren’t God’s works marvelous to us? Who can fully understand them?
Wasn’t creation itself a miracle — heaven and earth by his word, man from the dust, and miracles by his power?

f.w: man was created of the dust of the earth

n: Who can deny that Jesus and his apostles worked mighty miracles?

f.w: wrought by the hands of the apostles

n: If God worked miracles then, why would he stop and still be unchangeable? He does not change — if he did, he would not be God — so he remains a God of miracles.
The reason miracles stop is unbelief: people dwindle in disbelief, leave the right way, and don’t know the God they should trust. Miracles follow faith; they don’t create it.

f.w: because that they dwindle in unbelief

n: Whoever believes in Christ without doubting will receive what he asks the Father in Christ’s name — a promise to the whole earth.
Jesus said to his disciples, including the three who would remain, in the multitude’s hearing: go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.

f.w: Go ye into all the world

n: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved; whoever does not believe will be condemned.

f.w: he that believeth and is baptized shall be saved

n: Signs will follow believers: casting out devils, new tongues, protection from serpents and poison, and healing the sick by laying on of hands.

f.w: these signs shall follow them that believe

n: Whoever believes in Christ’s name without doubting will see Christ confirm all his words, everywhere on earth.
Who can fight God’s work, deny his words, or despise his children? Those who scorn his works will wonder and perish.

Don’t scorn or merely marvel — listen, ask the Father in Jesus’ name for what you need, don’t doubt, come to the Lord with all your heart as in ancient times, and work out your salvation with fear and trembling.

f.w: work out your own salvation with fear and trembling

n: Use this probationary life wisely: put away impurity, don’t ask for things just to satisfy your appetites, and ask with unshakable resolve to resist temptation and serve the living God.
Don’t be baptized or take the sacrament unworthily; do everything worthily in Christ’s name. Endure to the end and you will never be cast out.

f.w: partake not of the sacrament of Christ unworthily

n: Moroni speaks as if from the dead, knowing his words will reach us.

f.w: as though I spake from the dead

n: Don’t condemn him, his father, or earlier writers for their imperfections; thank God for revealing them so you can be wiser than they were.
The record was written in “reformed Egyptian,” a script modified over time by the Nephites to suit their language.

f.g: A modified Egyptian script; it took less space than Hebrew.

n: With larger plates they would have written in Hebrew, which they had also altered; then the record would have no imperfection. Writing space shaped their choices.

f.w: the Hebrew hath been altered by us also
f.g: Their language had changed over a thousand years.

n: The Lord knows what they wrote, and since no one else knows their language, he prepared a means of interpretation — the interpreters later used by Joseph Smith.
They write so as to rid their garments of their brethren’s blood — fulfilling their duty to warn, so they are not responsible for others’ sins.

f.w: rid our garments of the blood

n: The desire that their brethren be restored to knowledge of Christ matches the prayers of all the saints who lived in this land.

f.w: according to the prayers of all the saints

n: Moroni prays that Christ will answer those prayers according to their faith, that the Father will remember his covenant with Israel, and that he will bless them forever through faith in Jesus. Amen.
